meta_description: SRE & Reliability Engineering from Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, platforms and committed outcomes.

blocks.x: SRE & Reliability Engineering in production: what gets built, who owns each control, how the pilot widens into an industrial deployment, and the metrics that gate each phase.

Reliability is a negotiation, and SRE makes it explicit: user-journey SLOs instead of server vanity metrics, error budgets that gate feature velocity, and incident discipline (blameless review, action tracking, toil budgets) that converts failures into roadmap. We implement SRE on existing teams and platforms — SLO catalog construction, alert redesign from symptom-based paging, capacity planning, and chaos experiments that prove recovery paths.

The measurable outcomes are cultural as much as technical: paging volume drops when alerts point at symptoms, release confidence rises when error budgets arbitrate, and incident duration falls when playbooks, roles and comms are rehearsed. We leave behind the operating rhythm — reviews, budgets, postmortems — because reliability that depends on heroics is not reliability.

Delivery runs on one weekly rhythm for every program of this type. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline with your team: the current metric is measured, signed and stored as the reference for every later gate. Weeks 3–8 run the pilot on deliberately narrow scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, never quietly extended.
